name: Palladas of Alexandria
bio: Palladas of Alexandria was a grammarian and the last great epigrammatist of pagan Alexandria, known for bitter, satirical verse. The editor dates him to the fourth century AD; Paton's index says the fifth.
The epigrams here are those that Paton's first volume ascribes to him.

poems.title: Book V, 71
poems.author: Palladas of Alexandria
poems.text: Zenon, since you have married the daughter of Protomachus (first in fight) and of Nicomache (conquering in fight) you have war in your house. Search for a kind seducer, a Lysimachus (deliverer from fight) who will take pity on you and deliver you from Andromache (husband-fighter) the daughter of Protomachus.

poems.title: Book V, 72
poems.author: Palladas of Alexandria
poems.text: This is life, and nothing else is; life is delight ; away, dull care! Brief are the years of man. To-day wine is ours, and the dance, and flowery wreaths, and women. To-day let me live well; none knows what may be to-morrow.

poems.title: Book V, 257
poems.author: Palladas of Alexandria
poems.text: Now I condemn Zeus as a tepid lover, since he did not transform himself for this haughty fair’s sake. She is not second in beauty to Europa or Danae or tender Leda. But perhaps he disdains courtesans, for know they were maiden princesses he used to seduce.

poems.title: Book VI, 60
poems.author: Palladas of Alexandria
poems.text: Pamphile, in place of an ox and a golden offering, dedicated to Isis these glossy locks ; and the goddess takes more pleasure in them than Apollo in the gold that Croesus sent him from Lydia.

poems.title: Book VI, 61
poems.author: Palladas of Alexandria
poems.text: O heavenly razor, happy razor with which Pamphile shore her plaited tresses to dedicate them. It was no human smith that wrought thee, but beside the forge of Hephaestus the bright-snooded Grace (to use Homer’s words) took up the golden hammer and fashioned thee with her own hands.

poems.title: Book VI, 85
poems.author: Palladas of Alexandria
poems.text: His breaster and leggers and shield and spear and heller Captain Gordy dedicates to Timothy.
